scenes.visual: Host at the NES-style news desk; the screen behind her lights up with a pixel-art courthouse icon that pulses once, then a small question mark fades into a gavel silhouette.
scenes.narration: A federal appeals panel just doubted the government's own voter list.

scenes.visual: Full-screen pixel-art video-call courtroom: three small monitor windows labeled Bennett, Bumatay and Sanchez glow above a shared virtual bench; a digital calendar in the corner flips from Oct 25 to a blank 'no ruling yet' card.
scenes.narration: On Sunday, the Ninth Circuit held a rare emergency hearing on roughly 20,000 disputed mail ballots. Two of three judges, including a Trump appointee, challenged the Justice Department's authority and its alleged-noncitizen list. The panel took the case under submission, without ruling.

scenes.visual: Full-screen scene at a county clerk's desk: a government envelope marked 'DOJ' lands next to a sealed USB drive with a handwritten password note; a wall calendar on the desk flips from Oct 13 to Oct 15, circling the deadline date.
scenes.narration: The Justice Department sued California, saying over 20,000 mail ballots went to likely noncitizens. It gave officials two days to act, a deadline Secretary of State Shirley Weber called "a mere 48 hours." The county never opened the list, citing security rules.
scenes.source_plate: Source: DOJ complaint & CA Secretary of State letter · Oct 13-15

scenes.visual: Full-screen scene outside a federal courthouse: a separate wall calendar here flips from Oct 15 to Oct 19, where a small 'charges filed' stamp appears next to a plain case-file icon; no names or faces are shown.
scenes.narration: Four days later, the Justice Department charged 28 lawful permanent residents with election-related felonies, under what it called Operation Protect the Vote.

scenes.visual: Full-screen scene split into three vertical panels that slide in one at a time and each briefly highlight as its side speaks: Essayli at a podium marked 'DOJ' on the left, an unlabeled state-seal podium with two generic California-attorney icons in the middle, and Clarke at a microphone marked 'NAACP' on the right.
scenes.narration: The administration calls its count just a floor, warning that counting without checks permanently dilutes citizens' votes. California's lawyers call the list unverified and unlawful, warning it would disenfranchise voters instead. Voting rights groups, including the NAACP, call the push a suppression campaign, not fraud enforcement.

scenes.visual: Full-screen split-screen scene: a pixel-art world map zooms into the Middle East and UK on the left, where a plain wordless speech-bubble icon appears over a Newsom figure; it then pans to Canada on the right, where the same wordless bubble icon appears over a Carney figure; a thin dotted line connects the two panels.
scenes.narration: Outlets like Al Jazeera and The Guardian frame the fight as democratic backsliding, not a states'-rights dispute. Canadian coverage looks elsewhere: citizens charged in the same sweep, with Ottawa and Washington trading accusations over election interference.

scenes.visual: Full-screen scene: a courthouse door stays shut as a calendar page flips toward Oct 27 under a question-mark stamp; beside it, three mismatched bar-chart icons flicker without settling into one height.
scenes.narration: It's still unknown whether the Ninth Circuit will rule before Tuesday's hearing. Outlets also disagree on how many counties got DOJ's letters, and on a disputed birthplace statistic in the case.
scenes.source_plate: Source: NBC News, CBS News & LA County brief · Oct 20-24

scenes.visual: Host back at the news desk; the screen behind her shows a simple 'Sources: link in description' text card fading in as she delivers the closing line.
scenes.narration: Sources are in the description. Follow for what happens next.

tiktok.title: 9th Circuit judges doubt DOJ's CA ballot list
tiktok.summary: A Ninth Circuit panel heard a rare Sunday hearing on DOJ's bid to block roughly 20,000 California mail ballots, with two of three judges doubting its authority and list. No ruling yet before Tuesday's district hearing.
